ligand binding to clusters of receptors is reaction limited, and the transition to a diffusion-limited regime occurs only at low γ.

the binding kinetics of ligands to clusters of membrane-associated receptors can be described as a diffusion-controlled process only if the ligands bind to the clusters with a high rate constant (i.e. the process is reaction-limited).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the process of ligands binding by a disc-like cluster of membrane-associated receptor molecules is determined by the ratio of two time constants.

the process of binding by clustered receptors may be described by two dimensionless parameters, namely, γ ≡kD/a2, where k is the reaction rate constant, and the ratio of the lateral diffusion coefficient of a ligand to the diffusion coefficient of the ligand in the solution.

the diffusion-limited process of ligand-receptor interaction occurs when the ligand hits a cluster of membrane-bound receptors, and that the reaction-limited process occurs when the ligands are bound to the receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the process of ligands binding to the cluster of receptors can be described by the same theoretical model as the process of liganding by a single receptor.
the diffusion-limited process of ligand-binding by a cluster of membrane receptors is only possible if the ligands have a high affinity to the receptors.
the diffusion-limited regime is not observed in the process of ligands binding to clusters of membrane-associated receptors.
